report.summary: The OpenTelemetry Demo shop itself is up and serving: at the sampled times all 25 astronomy-shop Deployments report ready=available=1, all 29 pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts, all 4 nodes are Ready without memory/disk pressure, and the sampled frontend spans read from 13:10:38-13:10:51 carry HTTP 200 / gRPC status 0. The demo's own Kafka flows are healthy (accounting consumer on topic 'orders' lag 0 at 13:12:30; fraud-detection on 'orders' lag 1 at 13:13:47). The concrete failure is in the added orders pipeline: pod orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-fzkm9 started at 13:10:36, consumed orders-fulfillment offsets 0-19 successfully, then at 13:10:37 failed to parse the record at offset 20 (log: 'record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)') and by design logged 'partition processing paused at offset=20'. The consumer group orders-validator is STABLE but stuck at committed_offset 20 while the topic end offset keeps rising with order-stream's steady publishing: lag was 36 at 13:11:43 and 73 at 13:12:57, i.e. an unbounded, still-growing backlog and no further validation of orders. Nothing points to a crashed pod, broker outage, node pressure or an enabled flagd fault flag; what remains unproven is which producer wrote the malformed record at offset 20 (no producer pod/job is visible and the tool set exposes no message content), so the conclusion is partial with the topic holding the offending record as the identified fault location and orders-validator as the affected component.

claims.text: orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-fzkm9 logged at 13:10:36 'orders-validator started ... topic=orders-fulfillment', processed order_id=ORD-100000..ORD-100019 (committed_offset 1..20), then at 13:10:37 logged 'ERROR record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' and 'ERROR partition processing paused at offset=20'.
Consumer group orders-validator on topic orders-fulfillment was STABLE with one member assigned to partition 0, committed_offset 20, end_offset 56 and lag 36 messages at 13:11:43.
The orders-validator backlog grew from lag 36 (13:11:43) to total_lag 73 on orders-fulfillment at 13:12:57 while the group stayed STABLE with 1 member, i.e. no progress past the failed offset.
Topic orders-fulfillment exists with 1 partition, leader 1, replicas [1] and in-sync replicas [1], under_replicated=false and offline=false, so the broker side of that topic is not degraded.

order-stream-5c7cc84b47-tqh7r published one order per ~2 seconds from 13:10:34 to 13:10:50 (e.g. ORD-49B479E1C5ED at 13:10:34, ORD-501B4FA82169 at 13:10:50), so new valid messages keep appending behind the stalled offset and the lag keeps growing.

Deployment orders-validator runs 'python /scripts/consumer.py' (image ghcr.io/sregym/kafka-client:2.5.3-py3.12) from ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts mounted at /scripts, with env ORDERS_TOPIC=orders-fulfillment, OUTPUT_TOPIC=orders-processed, CONSUMER_GROUP=orders-validator and no readiness probe or resource requests/limits.

Every astronomy-shop Deployment has spec.replicas=1 with status readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1 (all 25 workloads, including orders-validator and order-stream), and every one of the 29 astronomy-shop pods is Running with all containers ready and restartCount 0.

The demo's own Kafka consumers are healthy: group accounting on topic orders had committed_offset 18 = end_offset 18, lag 0 with one assigned member (13:12:30), and group fraud-detection on topic orders had committed_offset 28, end_offset 29, lag 1 (13:13:47).

Sampled frontend spans read from 13:10:38-13:10:51 are successful, e.g. 'GET /api/recommendations' with http.status_code 200, 'POST /api/cart' with http.status_code 200, 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 and 'oteldemo.ProductReviewService/GetProductReviews' with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, with error_by_visible_tags=false on every span read.

The flagd flag definitions in ConfigMap flagd-config all have defaultVariant 'off' (including paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe), and runtime logs show the LLM flags inactive: 'llmRateLimitError feature flag: False' and 'llmInaccurateResponse feature flag: False'.
All four nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure=False and DiskPressure=False (queried at 13:13:44).

locust-fetcher's round reported fail_ratio 0.094 with 500 responses on /api/product-reviews/9SIQT8TOJO, /api/data/?contextKeys=travel, /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars, /api/cart (GET x2, POST x1) and /api/checkout (x2) at 13:10:12, while the later rounds at 13:10:32 and 13:10:42 report empty error lists and fail_ratio 0.0, so those 500s did not persist in the sampled rounds.

The consumer script in ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts validates each record with json.loads and, on any exception, logs 'record validation failed at offset=%d', logs 'partition processing paused at offset=%d', then loops sleeping forever logging 'partition remains paused at offset=%d' every 15 s instead of skipping the record; the same script signs records as records with an 'order_id' field, which the observed offset-20 error says the bad record lacks in valid form.

The record at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment is a malformed/poison message (its payload is not valid JSON) that blocks orders-validator at that offset; because the preceding 20 records carry sequential synthetic ids ORD-100000..ORD-100019 while order-stream emits random ORD-<12 hex> ids and only started publishing at 13:10:34, the bad record looks like it came from a seeding producer rather than from the deployed order-stream, but the producer itself is not visible in the cluster.

A second, contributing candidate is the consumer implementation itself: /scripts/consumer.py, taken from ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts, reacts to a single unparsable record by entering an infinite sleep loop ('partition remains paused at offset=%d') and never skips or dead-letters the record, which converts one bad message into a permanent partition stall.

The 500 responses recorded by locust-fetcher at 13:10:12 are a separate transient of the shop's first minute (load generator start-up, services still warming) and are not explained by the Kafka stall, since the frontend spans read at 13:10:38-13:10:51 all report http.status_code 200 / rpc.grpc.status_code 0 and the later locust rounds show no errors.

Rejected: an enabled flagd fault-injection flag (paymentFailure, cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, etc.) as the cause - every flag's defaultVariant is 'off' and the observed runtime flag readings are False.

Rejected: pod crash, OOM or restart-driven failure - all astronomy-shop pods are Running with ready containers and restartCount 0, with no terminated/waiting container reasons, and every Deployment reports 1/1 ready and available.

Rejected: Kafka broker/topic unavailability - topic orders-fulfillment has its leader and full ISR with under_replicated=false, and the other consumers of the same broker (accounting lag 0, fraud-detection lag 1) are keeping up.

Human follow-up: reset the orders-validator consumer past the poisoned offset (seek/commit beyond offset 20, or route offset 20 to a dead-letter topic) so consumption of orders-fulfillment resumes, then harden /scripts/consumer.py to skip and record an unparsable record instead of pausing the partition indefinitely.

Human follow-up: add lag alerting on group orders-validator/orders-fulfillment, because the stall produced no pod-level symptom (pod stayed Running and ready) and was only visible as monotonically growing consumer lag (36 -> 73 in 74 s).

gaps: The producer of the malformed record at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment is unidentified: no Job, CronJob or producer pod for it is visible (the jobs query returned no_data), and no tool exposes Kafka message content, so the exact payload and its author remain unverified (the char-34 parse position is only consistent with an invalid JSON value).

Queries for trace tags error=true on frontend/checkout and http.status_code="500" on frontend in 13:08:52-13:10:52 returned no_data (nothing matched); that empty result shows only that these queries matched nothing, so the absence of recorded error spans is unknown rather than established.

orders-processed could not be inspected for offsets: find_consumer_groups_by_topic returned no groups for it (no_data), and describe_topic exposes no end offset, so whether any order was ever validated and forwarded is unknown.

Load-generator and locust-fetcher pods appear in Loki logs until 13:10:42 (astronomy-shop) but are absent from the pod, Deployment and ReplicaSet listings at 13:11-13:12 (the replicaset query for them returned no_data); no event after 13:10:36 was returned, so their removal cannot be dated inside the authorized window and is recorded as unexplained rather than as impact.

No 24-hour baseline exists: the sampled metric views start at 13:10:52 (source_start_at), the namespace was (re)created at 13:09, and traces_span_metrics_calls_total only has series for 10 service_name values, so no latency trend or pre-incident comparison was possible; http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no data for this target.

The 500 responses reported by locust-fetcher at 13:10:12 on /api/cart, /api/checkout, /api/data and /api/product-reviews/9SIQT8TOJO could not be tied to any cause: Jaeger holds no sampled spans before 13:10:38 and no matching error lines were found in the frontend, checkout or product-reviews application logs.

A resourcequotas query in astronomy-shop returned no_data and a networkpolicies query across namespaces returned no_data; these queries matched nothing, so quota or network-policy involvement is unchecked rather than ruled out.
Secrets were not readable, so nothing depending on credentials (e.g. database connection strings, Grafana/flags secrets) was verified.

import json
import logging
import os
import signal
import time

from confluent_kafka import Consumer, Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("orders-validator")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
OUTPUT_TOPIC = os.environ.get("OUTPUT_TOPIC", "orders-processed")
GROUP = os.environ.get("CONSUMER_GROUP", "orders-validator")

_shutdown = False


def _request_shutdown(signum, frame):
    global _shutdown
    _shutdown = True


def process(value):
    obj = json.loads(value.decode("utf-8"))
    if "order_id" not in obj:
        raise ValueError("record has no 'order_id' field")
    return obj


def main():
    consumer = Consumer(
        {
            "bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP,
            "group.id": GROUP,
            "enable.auto.commit": False,
            "auto.offset.reset": "earliest",
            "max.poll.interval.ms": 86400000,
        }
    )
    out = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    consumer.subscribe([TOPIC])
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _request_shutdown)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _request_shutdown)
    log.info("orders-validator started bootstrap=%s topic=%s group=%s", BOOTSTRAP, TOPIC, GROUP)

    first = True
    while not _shutdown:
        msg = consumer.poll(1.0)
        if msg is None:
            continue
        if msg.error():
            log.warning("consumer error: %s", msg.error())
            continue

        if first:
            log.info("resuming partition at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            first = False

        try:
            order = process(msg.value())
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("record validation failed at offset=%d: %s", msg.offset(), exc)
            log.error("partition processing paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            blocked = 0
            while not _shutdown:
                time.sleep(1)
                blocked += 1
                if blocked % 15 == 0:
                    log.error("partition remains paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            break

        result = json.dumps(
            {"source_offset": msg.offset(), "order_id": order["order_id"]},
            separators=(",", ":"),
        )
        out.produce(OUTPUT_TOPIC, value=result.encode("utf-8"))
        out.flush(10)
        consumer.commit(message=msg, asynchronous=False)
        log.info("processed order_id=%s committed_offset=%d", order["order_id"], msg.offset() + 1)

    out.flush(10)
    consumer.close()
    log.info("orders-validator stopped")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import logging
import os
import time
import uuid

from confluent_kafka import Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("order-stream")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
INTERVAL = float(os.environ.get("PRODUCE_INTERVAL_SEC", "2.0"))


def main():
    producer = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    while True:
        order_id = "ORD-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12].upper()
        record = json.dumps({"order_id": order_id, "amount": 1 + int(uuid.uuid4().hex[:2], 16) % 7})
        producer.produce(TOPIC, value=record.encode("utf-8"))
        producer.poll(0)
        producer.flush(10)
        log.info("published order_id=%s", order_id)
        time.sleep(INTERVAL)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

service:
  extensions: [jaeger_storage, jaeger_query, healthcheckv2]
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]

    resource:
      service.name: jaeger
    metrics:
      level: detailed

        - periodic:

              otlp:
                protocol: http/protobuf

    logs:
      level: info
extensions:
  healthcheckv2:
    use_v2: true

      endpoint: 0.0.0.0:13133
  jaeger_query:
    storage:
      traces: memory_backend
      metrics: metrics_backend
    base_path: /jaeger/ui
  jaeger_storage:
    backends:

receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:JAEGER_HOST}:${env:JAEGER_GRPC_PORT}

processors:
  batch:

exporters:
  jaeger_storage_exporter:
    trace_storage: memory_backend
